text: Do you know NASA built a mirror so smooth that, if Earth were that smooth, its tallest mountain would be less than two metres high?
It's inside this. Chandra, built from NASA's own 3D model. It sees the sky in X-rays.
X-rays don't bounce off a normal mirror. They only skip off at a shallow angle, like a stone on water.
So Chandra has four pairs of long, barrel-shaped mirrors, nested one inside the other.
It's sharp enough to read a stop sign about twenty kilometres away.
In July nineteen ninety-nine, Space Shuttle Columbia carried it up. The heaviest cargo a shuttle ever launched.
Here's what it sees. This is the Crab Nebula, what's left of a star that exploded almost a thousand years ago.
In X-rays, it looks completely different. At its heart, a dead star spinning thirty times a second.
